prerequisites: Basic knowledge in network design, planning, and management

learning_outcomes.text: Allow the student to make informed selections of application technologies in the deployment of heterogeneous networks and apply them to a design of a communication infrastructure.
Analyze a client's needs when designing a network and establish a series of technical objectives.
Design a network from a logical perspective (topology, protocols, security strategies, etc.).
Design a network from a physical perspective (selection of devices and technologies).
Design and model communication networks and services integrating wired and wireless technologies.
Understand the tasks necessary to properly manage a corporate network (diagnosis and resolution of breakdowns, monitoring, device configuration, etc.).
Be able to choose the network management tools and protocols to use based on the needs of the network to be managed.
Quantify the impact of network management, its effectiveness, and how it can be improved.
Understand the weaknesses of communication networks, as well as the available security mechanisms to mitigate them.

syllabus_topics: VoIP networks and quality of service techniques
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.45 * (Written test) + 0.2 * (Group work) + 0.25 * (Practice reports) + 0.1 * (Self-assessment). To pass, the final grade must be 5 or higher. Additionally, the score obtained in the written test and group work cannot be less than 4 points. For the extraordinary examination, if group work and/or practice reports have a score of 4 or higher, the grade will be kept; otherwise, they must be corrected and resubmitted. A written test on theoretical content must also be passed. The final grade for the extraordinary examination is 0.5 * (Written test) + 0.2 * (Group work) + 0.3 * (Practice reports). For differentiated evaluation, final in-person exams for theory and practice will be conducted. The final grade for differentiated evaluation is 0.7 * (Theory test) + 0.3 * (Practice test).
